extracted.intended_audience: registrants (issuer companies), corporate accountants, auditors, and securities lawyers preparing SEC filings for business combinations (e.g., reverse acquisitions, carve-outs)
extracted.subtask_short: SEC financial reporting for business combinations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for the form, content, audit, and filing timing of financial statements and disclosures required by the SEC (Regulation S-X, Form 8-K, Form 10, Rule 3-05, SAB Topic 1.B.1, etc.) in connection with acquisitions, reverse acquisitions, carve-outs, and portions of businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of financial statement periods for Form 8-K
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statement periods required in the Form 8-K are determined as of the earlier of the Form 8-K’s filing date or due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The age and number of periods to include depends on whether the accounting acquirer would qualify as an SRC. If the operating company would qualify as an SRC, Article 8 applies (two years permitted). If not, Article 3 applies (two or three years required). If both shell and operating company qualify as EGCs and the shell hasn't filed its first Form 10-K, two years permitted; otherwise three years required. Age requirements may differ between Form 8-K and Form 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amended Form 8-K is required to update pre-acquisition financials
rubrics_metrics.description: If pre-acquisition financial statements filed in the initial Form 8-K do not include the operating company’s most recently completed full fiscal year or latest interim period, the registrant must file an amended Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amended Form 8-K must include all information about the operating company that would be included in an annual or periodic report (e.g., Form 10-K or 10-Q), including financial statements for the most recently completed pre-acquisition annual (or interim) period. For a non-accelerated filer, if the missing period is annual the amended Form 8-K is due within 90 days of the operating company’s year-end; if interim, due within 45 days of the interim period-end. The registrant must also continue to file its own periodic reports for periods ending before consummation as they become due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant financial statements after consummation (reverse recapitalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: The operating company's pre-acquisition financial statements filed on Form 8-K become the registrant's (predecessor's) historical financial statements; shell company historical statements for periods prior to acquisition may not be required in future Forms 10-K/10-Q if the registrant had only nominal income statement activity before the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the initial Form 8-K includes financial statements that comply with Form 10 content, an amended Form 8-K may not be required; registrant still must file its Form 10-K including audited statements for its own periods. If initial Form 8-K does not comply, the registrant may be required to file an amended Form 8-K and include the operating company's most recently completed pre-acquisition annual period as the registrant’s first annual report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit requirements for financial statements in reverse recapitalization with a public shell
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of an operating company determined to be the predecessor of a nonoperating public shell must be audited under PCAOB standards when filed by the public shell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC staff treats the transaction as equivalent to an IPO of the target; the Form 8-K must include all content required by a Form 10 initial registration statement (i.e., financial statements meeting Reg S-X). The auditor of the accounting acquirer must be independent under PCAOB/SEC independence rules for all years required to be filed on the Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing requirement for reverse acquisition with domestic registrant that is not a shell
rubrics_metrics.description: A reverse acquisition involving a domestic registrant that is not a shell company requires a Form 8-K reporting the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike a reverse recap with a shell company, the domestic registrant that is not a shell may apply the 71-calendar day extension to file required legal acquiree financial statements and pro forma information under Item 9.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Form 8-K Items for reverse acquisitions (domestic registrant not shell)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Form 8-K must include the information listed in the specified items when reporting such a reverse acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items required include: Item 2.01 (Information about the completed merger transaction), Item 4.01 (Information about a change in registrant's certifying accountant), Item 5.01 (Information about a change in control of the registrant), Item 5.03 (Information about a change in fiscal year of the registrant), and Item 9.01 (Financial statements of the operating company and pro forma financial information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements required for reverse acquisition with domestic registrant (Rule coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements for all periods required by S-X Rules 3-01 through 3-04 (including pre-acquisition financial statements) must be on file for the predecessor when the legal acquiree is the accounting acquirer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 3-06 (permitting filing of nine- to twelve-month statements to satisfy one year) does not apply to the financial statements of the accounting acquirer in a reverse acquisition. See guidance on Rule 3-06 for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit standards for accounting acquirer in reverse acquisition with domestic registrant not a shell
rubrics_metrics.description: A private operating company that is the accounting acquirer in a reverse acquisition with a public operating company is not considered an 'issuer' for its pre-acquisition financial statements included in related filings; these pre-acquisition statements can be audited under AICPA standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The auditor must comply with AICPA independence standards applicable to those periods. However, once the accounting acquirer's financial statements become the historical financial statements of the registrant/issuer (e.g., in a later Form 10-K or registration statement), any reissuance or presentation as issuer will require all periods presented to be audited in accordance with PCAOB standards; PCAOB/SEC auditing and independence requirements will then apply and may be accelerated when a Securities Act registration statement is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-05(e) qualifying conditions for abbreviated financial statements (net assets constituting a business)
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquired business's financial statements may be abbreviated if the business meets all qualifying conditions in Rule 3-05(e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying conditions include: (i) total assets and total revenues of the acquired business constitute 20% or less of the seller's corresponding amounts (after intercompany eliminations) for the most recently completed fiscal year; (ii) separate financial statements for the business have not previously been prepared; (iii) the acquired business was not a separate entity, subsidiary, operating segment, or division during the required periods; and (iv) the seller has not maintained distinct and separate accounts necessary to present full financial statements and it is impracticable to prepare such statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirements for abbreviated financial statements under S-X Rule 3-05(e)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If abbreviated financial statements are used for an acquired business, certain presentation rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation may include a balance sheet as a statement of assets acquired and liabilities assumed; the statement of comprehensive income must include expenses incurred by or on behalf of the acquired business during pre-acquisition periods (but may omit corporate overhead, interest for debt not assumed, and income tax expense) and must have a title indicating omitted expenses; notes must disclose (A) types of omitted expenses and reasons for exclusion, (B) explanation of impracticability of preparing statements that include omitted expenses, (C) description of how presented statements are not indicative of future condition/results due to omitted expenses, and (D) information about operating, investing and financing cash flows to the extent available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil and gas producing activities — additional disclosures and permitted abbreviated format
rubrics_metrics.description: If the acquired business includes significant oil-and-gas-producing activities, special disclosures are required for each full year of operations presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures may present ASC Topic 932 items as unaudited supplemental information. If prior year reserve studies are not available, reserves may be computed using production and new discovery quantities with method disclosed in a footnote. Financial statements under Reg S-X may consist only of statements of revenues and expenses that exclude certain noncomparable expenses (depreciation, depletion, amortization, corporate overhead, income taxes, interest not assumed) if (i) acquisition generates substantially all revenues from oil and gas producing activities and (ii) Rule 3-05(e)(1) qualifying conditions are met. If that format is used, the paragraph (e)(2)(iii) disclosures must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content options for financial statements of a portion of a larger entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements for a component of a larger business should present information reflecting the acquired component's operating history as if it had operated on a stand-alone basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include carve-out special purpose financial statements or abbreviated financial statements when Rule 3-05(e) conditions are met. Component financial statements must meet the same period and age requirements under S-X Rule 3-05 as full financial statements. If carve-out or abbreviated statements cannot be provided (e.g., audit impossible, lack of records), the registrant should seek an SEC staff waiver to provide alternative financial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to determine appropriate form and content for partial-entity acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Key considerations are defining the business being acquired and assessing the substance and purpose of the acquisition and the availability of financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider (i) the substance of the acquisition transaction, (ii) intended purpose and use of the financial statements, and (iii) availability of financial information of the acquired business. Also evaluate whether the financial statements must meet requirements beyond Rule 3-05 (e.g., initial registration statements, Rule 144A offerings, spin-offs). When carve-out or abbreviated statements will represent registrant financials in an initial registration, full Reg S-X financials may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance testing when only a portion of an entity is acquired
rubrics_metrics.description: When an acquired business was part of a larger entity, the registrant determines significance as required by S-X Rule 3-05 using the closest available financial information to full statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asset test: compare proportionate interest in total assets of the acquired business to registrant's total assets; if only less-than-full financial information or carve-outs available, compare book value of assets acquired. Income test: compare income or loss from continuing operations before income taxes attributable to controlling interests of the acquired business with registrant income; if only carve-outs or partial info available, apply income test literally using revenues less direct costs (or similar) compared to registrant's income. Do not adjust registrant's income to exclude corporate overhead. If literal application yields unreasonable result, seek SEC staff relief/waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carve-out financial statements — when acceptable and required explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If impracticable to prepare full financial statements of an acquired business, the SEC staff will accept audited carve-out financial statements, but the registrant's filing must explain the impracticability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Carve-out financial statements' are special separate statements derived from the parent's financials that generally reflect all assets and liabilities of the acquired business and include reasonable allocation of indirect costs like corporate overhead. The SEC's rules do not directly define carve-outs, but the staff expects compliance with SAB Topic 1.B.1 on allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate circumstances for carve-out financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Carve-out financial statements are appropriate when the acquired business represents a discrete activity with specifically identifiable assets and liabilities and a reasonable basis exists to allocate items not specifically identifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include product lines or domestic operations separable from other operations; however, definition acceptable for Rule 3-05 purposes may not be appropriate if financials will be used stand-alone in an IPO or spin-off. Legal form of restructuring (capital contribution vs net asset transfer) can affect required content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical content of carve-out financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Carve-out financial statements generally include a balance sheet; statements of operations (through net income); cash flows; stockholders' equity (separately or in a note); comprehensive income; and related notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes must disclose basis of presentation, methods used for allocation, and any additional information necessary for investors. The appropriate level of carve-out depends on how the acquired business is defined and the intended use of the financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of expenses (including taxes) in carve-out financial statements — general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: When expenses are not specifically identifiable to the acquired business, the registrant allocates expenses based on reasonable assumptions to reflect all expenses of the acquired business in the carve-out statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff expects compliance with SAB Topic 1.B.1. If expenses were not previously charged to the business, the staff has required revision to include such costs (examples: officer and employee salaries; rent or depreciation; advertising; accounting and legal services; other SG&A). When reasonable allocation methods are used (e.g., incremental or proportional), disclose the allocation method in the notes and include management's assertion that the method is reasonable. If related-party arrangements exist, footnote disclosure of management's estimate of what expenses would have been on a stand-alone basis should be provided when practicable and materially different.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation when prior carve-out statements were previously reported by independent accountants
rubrics_metrics.description: When a subsidiary's financial statements have been previously reported externally and used beyond internal purposes, staff may accept a presentation that shows previously reported income before tax followed by adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such presentation can show income before tax as previously reported, then adjustments for expenses not previously allocated, income taxes, and adjusted net income for each year for which an income statement was required when that adjusted basis produced materially different results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income tax considerations for carve-outs and related disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff considers it material for investors to understand the effect on income if the registrant had not been included in a consolidated income tax return with its parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a parent has sold interests in subsidiaries but retained inclusion in consolidated tax returns, disclosures may be required to show the effect on income had the subsidiary been taxed separately; further guidance continues in subsequent sections (not included in this chunk).
